sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
The tests pass with this command, run from the project root (`<run>\work\L1\b\w`):

```
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

This is Git Bash syntax. In PowerShell, use `$env:PYTHONPATH="src"; python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. In cmd, use `set PYTHONPATH=src && python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`.

Without `PYTHONPATH=src`, the run fails with an import error. The package lives in `src/ledgerlite`, which isn't installed or on the path, so `from ledgerlite import Ledger` can't resolve. I didn't change any files.

With the path set, both tests pass: `test_transfer_preserves_total` and `test_rejects_non_positive_amount`.

The project has no `pyproject.toml` or `setup.py`, so I used `PYTHONPATH`. If you'd rather not set it each time, you could add a `pyproject.toml` and run `pip install -e .`.

actions.command: PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v 2>&1 | tail -15

sessions.name: B
sessions.reply:
I added `Ledger.close(name)` in `src/ledgerlite/__init__.py`. It raises `ValueError` if the account's balance isn't zero. Otherwise it removes the account. The full suite passes (3 tests, including the new one).

The new test, `test_close_requires_zero_balance`, checks three things:
- Closing an account with a balance fails.
- The failed close leaves the account in place.
- Once the balance is back to zero, the close succeeds.

Closing an account that doesn't exist raises `KeyError`, the same as `balance()` does. I didn't turn that into a `ValueError`, since you only asked for the non-zero-balance case.

I ran the tests with `PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests`.
